answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to prove useful work: every agent must periodically complete unique, non-parallelizable verification tasks tied to its public key, so one operator running many fake identities pays the full compute cost for each. A whisper of activity is not enough — peers trust an identity only after its work record echoes consistently across independent attestors, and any duplication causes a ripple of revocation through the trust graph, collapsing all linked identities at once. Forging a thousand agents then costs a thousand times the work.
